capitals.name: Jolbon (Huanren)

correction.text: Jolbon, where Jumong 'founded Goguryeo in 37 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year, one year before Cliopatria's first shape: the page has 'Establishment: 37 BCE' at Jolbon, and the conquests of Biryu (36 BCE), Haengin (33 BCE) and Northern Okjeo (28 BCE) follow. The extent is a placeholder radius round the first capital.

The Goguryeo page gives no area figure (its only extent statement is undated: 'At its peak of power, Goguryeo encompassed most of the Korean peninsula and large parts of Manchuria'), so the infobox comparison is not possible. Cliopatria's 93,675 km2 for -36..22 (Jolbon, the upper Yalu and Tumen) is the shape after the early conquests the page dates to 36, 33 and 28 BCE; the ledger carries them as gains. The first attack on the Xuantu Commandery is dated 12 CE (no land changes).

minus.text: Nangnang (Lelang), 'northwestern Korea', which the page has Goguryeo destroying in 37

correction.text: the Cliopatria 23 shape without the Pyongyang and Hwanghae area, valid 23..36

The Daemusin page dates Dongbuyeo 22, Gaema-guk 26, 'defeated the Nakrang Kingdom in northwestern Korea in 32' and 'destroyed Nangnang in 37'; so the southern part belongs to 37..44 only (next keyframe), and 23..36 is the shape without it. Within 23..36 the 22 and 26 conquests lie along the Yalu and in the north-east, where the shape's bbox does not change.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 23 shape unchanged, with Nangnang, for 37..44 (years changed only)

correction.text: the Cliopatria 43 shape unchanged, valid 45..59 (years changed only: Nangnang was lost in 44)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria drops the south in 43 (-62,227 km2); the page has the Han army recapturing Nangnang in 44, so this shape holds from 45, not 43.

The Goguryeo page gives no area figure (its only extent statement is undated: 'At its peak of power, Goguryeo encompassed most of the Korean peninsula and large parts of Manchuria'), so the infobox comparison is not possible. Taejo (reign 53 to 146 or 121) 'conquered the states of Eastern Okjeo in 56' and built a fortress in the Liaodong Commandery in 55; he 'attacked Chinese border regions in 105, 111, and 118' and allied with Mahan and the Yemaek to attack Liaodong in 122, 'greatly expanding the realm of Goguryeo' (no land named, Cliopatria's western bbox does not move). Okjeo is carried as a vassal tint (ledger 56), not as part of this shape.

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo, which remains a tributary state until the early 5th century

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria adds 31,977 km2 in 154, almost exactly the 31,981 km2 of its Dong-okjeo shape, which ends 153. The Okjeo page has Taejo 'reduced Okjeo to a tributary' in the 1st or 2nd century and Gwanggaeto conquering it completely only 'in early 5th century'; so Okjeo stays a separate (vassal) state, ledger 56 and 401, and is taken out of this shape.

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo

The Wei page records no formal boundary change for 245 to 248, but says Goguryeo lost much of its economic base in Okjeo and Ye.

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo

correction.text: Goguryeo with Lelang, without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo

keyframe_review.note: Same shape without Dong-okjeo (see 154); +26 km2 is boundary noise. The page has Gogugyang invading Later Yan in 385 and Baekje in 386 without naming land. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Hamgyong coast of Dong-okjeo

keyframe_review.note: Same shape without Dong-okjeo (see 154); +46 km2 boundary noise. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Goguryeo with Baekje's ten walled cities, without Dong-okjeo and the Ye (valid 392..394)

keyframe_review.note: +31,200 km2 in 392. The Eastern Ye page and the Dongye dossier date the annexation of the Ye to 'early 5th-century' (ledger 401), so the Ye land is taken out until then; the Baekje part is the Gwanggaeto page's '392: ... capturing 10 walled cities' (Baekje loses 1,797 km2 in 392). Dong-okjeo also stays a vassal (see 154).

correction.text: Goguryeo without Dong-okjeo and the Ye, valid 395..400; the Cliopatria shape as drawn applies from 401

keyframe_review.note: +4,652 km2 in 395, matching Baekje's -4,676 km2: 'Baekje ... was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River' (Gwanggaeto page, 395); 396 the Baekje capital taken and Asin 'submitted'. Dong-okjeo and the Ye are taken out until 401 (see 392); the shape as drawn holds from 401.

Dong-okjeo and the Ye are inside from 401 (ledger 401: 'early 5th-century'). 402: Gwanggaeto 'returned Prince Silseong' and appointed him king of Silla; Silla is carried as a vassal (ledger 400). 400-406 fighting with Later Yan: 402 'conquered the prominent fortress called 宿軍城 near the capital of Later Yan', 405 and 406 Later Yan attacks in Liaodong beaten off.

+55,162 km2 in 407, bbox west to 121.03E: 'Gwanggaeto conquered all of Liaodong' after the 406 Later Yan attack (Gwanggaeto page; 'Goguryeo controlled Liaodong until the mid-late 7th century'). Later Yan's own shape loses 54,888 km2 in 407.
+105,909 km2 in 410, bbox north to 45.10N and east to 132.60E: Gwanggaeto 'attacked Eastern Buyeo to the northeast' in 410; the Goguryeo page says he 'annexed much of Buyeo'. Page area not given.

No change 426..475. 427: capital moved to Pyongyang (Jangsu page: 'a more suitable region to grow into a burgeoning metropolitan capital'); 435 formal relations with Northern Wei; 438 the Northern Yan emperor imprisoned.
+8,404 km2 in 476, matching Baekje's -8,504 km2: 475 Jangsu 'easily captured the city of Wiryeseong and slew Gaero'; 'The war gave Goguryeo more or less total control of the Han River valley'.

+18,364 km2 in 480 with no matching loss in any Cliopatria neighbour. The Jangsu page dates two Silla gains: 468, expanding into parts of Gangwon Province, and 489, capturing 7 walled cities in parts of North Gyeongsang Province; Cliopatria books them (probably) together in 480, and Silla's own shape does not change before 534. The ledger carries the page's years.
-49 km2, boundary noise. 491: Jangsu dies; under Munja (491 to 519) Goguryeo 'completely annexed Buyeo' (Goguryeo page, no year within the reign). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 523 shape unchanged, valid 523..550 (years changed only)

keyframe_review.note: Holds 523..550. 551: 'Baekje regained its original capital in 551' (Seong page); the Han River valley is lost to Silla in 553 (see the next two entries). Shape unchanged for 523..550.

minus.text: the Seoul region, Baekje's original capital regained in 551

correction.text: Goguryeo without the Seoul region, valid 551..552

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 551..552: Baekje, allied with Silla, retakes its old capital area: 'Baekje regained its original capital in 551' (Seong page); the Goguryeo page has the alliance in 551. The Seoul region is out of the Goguryeo shape for these two years.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 555 shape unchanged, valid 553..611 (years changed only)

keyframe_review.note: -48,325 km2 in 555, matching Silla's +48,888 km2; the Goguryeo page has 'Silla ... took possession of the entire Han River valley in 553'. The shape holds from 553, not 555. Silla's Cliopatria shape reaches 40.16N (the east coast), which the pages opened do not explain: a gap-filler should open the Silla–Goguryeo pages.

-52,939 km2 for 612..616 (Sui +19,139 km2, bbox east to 126.36E). The Sui war page says Yeongyang 'gave up the buffer zone that he had acquired after the war of 598' before the 612 campaign, which fits a smaller shape; it records no captured fortress ('By June ... not a single castle, fortress, or citadel has fallen to Sui').

+52,939 km2: the buffer zone is back in 617, the year after the last Sui campaign page entry (614: 'Emperor Yang accepted Yeongyang's offer of peace and withdrew Sui troops'). No opened page dates the recovery; confidence 1 in the ledger. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 634 shape (360,601 km2), the same outline as 617..632, valid for 633 as well

keyframe_review.note: A one-year shape of 234,104 km2 (-126,496 km2) with no event on any opened page; the Tang Cliopatria shape grows by 2.5 M km2 in 633 (Mongolian Plateau) and seems to overlay the north of Goguryeo. The Goguryeo–Tang War page starts in 645. Use the 617 and 634 outline.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 634 shape unchanged, valid 634..668 only; 669..673 is the Tang Protectorate General to Pacify the East

keyframe_review.note: Holds to 668 only: 'besieged and conquered Pyongyang on 22 October' 668. The 645 campaign (Gaimou, Liaodong, Baiyan) was withdrawn on 13 October 645 and changed no border; 661-662 Pyongyang held; 667 Xin Fortress captured. Cliopatria continues the shape to 673 though the Tang protectorate was set up in 668/669 and the Silla–Tang page has Goguryeo uprisings every year 670 to 673. correction.text: empty: remove this shape (an outline minus itself); the land is Tang protectorate to 676, then Silla south of the Taedong and Tang north of it

keyframe_review.note: A 148 km2 sliver near 125.2-125.5E, 37.64-37.77N for 674..681 that no opened page explains: the Goguryeo page has Bojang crowned 'King of Joseon' by the Tang in 677 and exiled in 681, and Anseung founding Bodeok (no year, no place). Remove it; the land belongs to the Tang protectorate until 676 and the Taedong line afterwards.

ledger.note: 37 BCE: Jumong founds Goguryeo at Jolbon. The page has Jumong 'founded Goguryeo in 37 BC' (infobox 'Establishment: 37 BCE'), with Jolbon as capital 37 BCE-3 CE; the page does not locate Jolbon, so the Huanren placeholder is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the tribal states of Biryu (location not on the page)

ledger.note: 36 BCE: Jumong 'conquered the tribal states of Biryu'. The page does not say where Biryu lay; the radius round Jolbon is a placeholder.
33 BCE: Goguryeo conquers Haengin (spelled Haeng-in on the page); the page does not locate it, so the radius round Jolbon is a placeholder.

region.text: Northern Okjeo (Buk-okjeo), 'the Duman River region' (Okjeo page)

ledger.note: 28 BCE: Goguryeo takes Northern Okjeo. The Goguryeo page has it conquered; the Okjeo page says 'In 28 BCE, King Dongmyeong sent Bu Wiyeom to attack the Northern Okjeo' and puts Buk-okjeo in 'the Duman River region'.
3: the capital moves from Jolbon to Gungnae. Infobox: 'Jolbon (37 BCE–3 CE)', 'Gungnae (3–427)'.

region.text: Dongbuyeo (Eastern Buyeo); the page names no place

ledger.note: 22: Daemusin annexes Dongbuyeo. 'He annexed Dongbuyeo and killed its king Daeso in 22 AD.' The page gives no location for Dongbuyeo; the radius on the Tumen at Yanji is a placeholder (the Gwanggaeto page puts Eastern Buyeo 'to the northeast'). Confidence 2 (reviewer jk-02-b): the year is the page's, the place is the placeholder.
26: Goguryeo conquers Gaema-guk on the Yalu. 'In 26 AD he conquered Gaema-guk, along the Amnok River, and later conquered Guda-guk' (no year for Guda).

32: Daemusin's war for Nangnang (Lelang) opens. 'He also defeated the Nakrang Kingdom in northwestern Korea in 32.' The page also has a Chinese attack repelled in 28 and Prince Hodong sent against the Nangnang Commandery (undated).
37: Goguryeo destroys Nangnang. 'He destroyed Nangnang in 37.' The page calls it Nangnang, not Lelang; the Pyongyang and Hwanghae area is the researcher's reading of 'northwestern Korea'.
37: the fighting over Nangnang ends in Goguryeo's favour until the Han counter-stroke in 44.

region.text: Nangnang (Lelang), recaptured by Eastern Han in 44

ledger.note: 44: the Han take Nangnang back. 'an Eastern Han army sent by Emperor Guangwu of Han, captured it in 44.'

region.text: the Ye (Dongye) of the Korean east coast

ledger.note: 53 on: the Ye become Goguryeo's vassals. The Goguryeo page has Taejodae (53-146) 'conquering the Okjeo and Dongye tribes' without a year; 53, his accession, is a bridging date. The Eastern Ye page: 'Ye appears in history as a vassal state of Goguryeo' (undated); the Wei page has the Ye under Wei's Lelang and Daifang after 245.

56: Taejo conquers Eastern Okjeo. 'conquered the states of Eastern Okjeo in 56.' The Okjeo page has Taejo 'reduced Okjeo to a tributary, which delivered local products to Goguryeo' in the 1st or 2nd century, so Okjeo is drawn as a vassal tint, not as Goguryeo territory.

region.text: Hwando, the capital destroyed by Wei in 244

ledger.note: 244: Wei's Guanqiu Jian takes Hwando. 'The Wei army took Hwando, where it wrought much destruction, slaughtering and capturing thousands of people', and 'The king and his family fled the capital'; Wang Qi's pursuit reached South Okjeo, where the Okjeo tribes 'were all defeated'. Goguryeo raided Xi'anping in 242.
245: Wei withdraws. Guanqiu Jian returned to You Province 'in around June 245'; in 247 the king relocated his capital to a 'walled town in the plain'.

region.text: Lelang, which the page says reached 'as far south as the Han River' (South Korean scholars limit it to Pyongyang and Hwanghae)

ledger.note: 313: Micheon absorbs Lelang. Goguryeo annexed Lelang under King Micheon (Lelang page; month not given); the Goguryeo page has Micheon 'conquered and absorbed' Lelang, the last Chinese commandery. 314: Micheon attacked Daifang.

region.text: the ten walled cities taken from Baekje in 392

ledger.note: 392: Gwanggaeto opens on Baekje. He attacked with 40,000 troops, 'capturing 10 walled cities'; the page names no city, so the region is the land Baekje's Cliopatria shape loses in 392.

region.text: the Han River heartland round Wiryeseong

ledger.note: 392-396: the war for Baekje's Han River heartland. 393 and 394 Asin 'was defeated' twice; 395 Baekje 'was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River'.
395: Baekje is pushed back to Wiryeseong. 'was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River' after another Goguryeo victory.

region.text: the Han River heartland round Wiryeseong

ledger.note: 396: Gwanggaeto takes the Baekje capital. Asin 'submitted to him', surrendering 'a prince and 10 government ministers'; Baekje keeps the Han valley until 475, so the page's 'subjugated' is not drawn as territory.

region.text: Silla as a protectorate of Goguryeo

ledger.note: 400: Gwanggaeto answers Silla's appeal. The page gives 399 ('dispatched 50,000 expeditionary troops, ... securing Silla as a de facto protectorate') and 400 ('influenced Silla as a suzerain'); 'Gaya declined and never recovered'. 402: he 'returned Prince Silseong' and made him king of Silla.

401: the Ye vassalage ends in annexation. 'In early 5th-century, however, King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo annexed Ye'; 401 is the Dongye dossier's bridging year for 'early 5th-century'. 'A small part of Ye in the south was absorbed into Silla.'

region.text: the Ye land (South Hamgyong, Kangwon, Gangwon)

ledger.note: 401: Goguryeo annexes the Ye. 'King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo annexed Ye, leading to Goguryeo's domination of the entire northern portion of the Korean peninsula'; the year is bridging (the page says 'early 5th-century'); Cliopatria already gives the land to Goguryeo from 392.
401: the Okjeo tributary state ends. 'In early 5th century, Okjeo was completely conquered by Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo'; 401 is the bridging year shared with the Ye.
401: Goguryeo takes Okjeo outright (see the preceding event).

region.text: Liaodong, where Later Yan attacked in 405 and 406

ledger.note: 405: Later Yan attacks Goguryeo's Liaodong fortresses (遼東城) and is beaten; 402 Goguryeo had taken a fortress near the Later Yan capital.

region.text: all of Liaodong (the 407 increment, bbox west to 121.03E)

ledger.note: 406: Gwanggaeto holds all of Liaodong. After Later Yan's second defeat (406) 'Gwanggaeto conquered all of Liaodong'; the page adds 'Goguryeo controlled Liaodong until the mid-late 7th century'. The region is the land Cliopatria adds in 407.
406: the Liaodong fighting ends in Goguryeo's favour.

region.text: Eastern Buyeo to the north-east (the 410 increment)

ledger.note: 410: Gwanggaeto takes Eastern Buyeo. 'Gwanggaeto attacked Eastern Buyeo to the northeast'; the Goguryeo page: he 'annexed much of Buyeo'. The region is the land Cliopatria adds in 410.
427: the capital moves to Pyongyang (Goguryeo page: 'moved the capital in 427 to Pyongyang'; Jangsu page: from Gungnae Fortress).
468: Jangsu invades Silla, expanding into parts of Gangwon Province. The part of Gangwon that Silla held is the researcher's reading.
468 at the latest: Silla is no longer a Goguryeo protectorate. The pages give no end for the 400 relation; Jangsu's invasion of Silla in 468 is the first sign of enmity.

region.text: the Han River valley round Wiryeseong

ledger.note: 475: Jangsu takes Wiryeseong. 'Jangsu easily captured the city of Wiryeseong and slew Gaero'; 'The war gave Goguryeo more or less total control of the Han River valley'. Baekje moved to Ungjin.
489: Jangsu invades Silla again, capturing 7 walled cities and expanding into parts of North Gyeongsang Province.

region.text: the Buyeo lands on the Songhua River

ledger.note: On Munja's accession (491 to 519) Goguryeo 'completely annexed Buyeo'. The page gives no year inside the reign; 491 is the bridging date. Jangsu 'reached the Songhua River' (413-491).

region.text: the Seoul region, Baekje's original capital

ledger.note: 551: Baekje retakes its old capital. 'Baekje regained its original capital in 551' with the aid of Silla and Gaya.
551: Baekje and Silla 'entered into an alliance to attack Goguryeo'; the Han River valley is fought over until Silla holds it in 553.
553: Silla takes the Han River valley. 'Silla took possession of the entire Han River valley in 553.' The page does not say whether from Goguryeo or Baekje; the land is the Cliopatria loss of 555.
553: the Han River valley fighting ends with Silla in possession; 554 Baekje's King Seong is killed in the retaliatory strike.

region.text: the buffer zone acquired after the war of 598

ledger.note: 612 (Cliopatria's year): the buffer zone is given up. Yeongyang 'gave up the buffer zone that he had acquired after the war of 598'; the page does not date the cession or say to whom. Cliopatria gives Sui only 19,139 km2 of the 52,939 km2.

region.text: Liaodong and the Liao River crossing

ledger.note: 612: the Sui army crosses the Liao. 'The army began to depart in early 612'; the Sui built bridges, crossed, and besieged Yodong; 'By June ... not a single castle ... has fallen to Sui'. Salsu: 'only 2,700 returned' of 305,000.
614: peace. 'Emperor Yang accepted Yeongyang's offer of peace and withdrew Sui troops from Goguryeo's territory.' 613 a second Liaodong invasion failed.
617 (Cliopatria's year): the buffer zone is back in Goguryeo's hands as Sui crumbles; no opened page dates it.

645: Taizong invades. 'Gaimou (Kaemo) ... fell after only 11 days' (siege from 16 May); 7 June a 40,000-man relief army crushed; 16 June 'the fall of Liaodong to the Tang forces'; 27 June Baiyan surrendered.
645: the Tang withdraw. Taizong 'was compelled to order a withdrawal from Goguryeo on October 13' after Ansi Fortress held; no border changed.

667: the last Tang offensive. 'In early 667, a Tang invasion of Goguryeo was launched with Li Shiji at its head' after Yŏn Kaesomun's death in 666; the Goguryeo page: 'captured Shin/Xin Fortress' in 667.
668: Pyongyang falls (see dissolve).

22 October 668: Pyongyang falls and Goguryeo ends. Tang and Silla forces 'besieged and conquered Pyongyang on 22 October'; 'the Tang government established the Protectorate General to Pacify the East' (669 on this page, 668 on the Silla–Tang page, based in Pyongyang). 670-673 yearly uprisings; 676 Silla holds the land south of the Taedong; 677 Bojang 'King of Joseon'; 681 exiled.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Han war over Lelang
wars.outcome: Goguryeo destroyed Nangnang in 37; an Eastern Han army sent by Emperor Guangwu recaptured it in 44.
wars.note: The page dates the Chinese attack to 28 and Prince Hodong's attack on the Nangnang Commandery to no year.

wars.name: Taejo's border wars with Han Liaodong
wars.outcome: Raids on Chinese border regions in 105, 111 and 118; an allied attack on Liaodong in 122 with the Mahan confederacy and the Yemaek 'greatly expanding the realm of Goguryeo'; peace with Han in the following year; another major attack in 146.
wars.note: No land is named; Cliopatria's western bbox does not move before 407.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Wei War
wars.outcome: Wei sacked Hwando in 244 and pursued the king into Okjeo; the army returned to You Province in about June 245; Goguryeo kept its land but lost much of its economic base in Okjeo and Ye.
wars.note: Begun by Goguryeo's raid on Xi'anping in 242 after the 238 alliance against Gongsun Yuan. The page: Wei kept Lelang, Daifang and the Liaodong commanderies it took in 238.

wars.name: Former Yan invasion of Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Former Yan 'attacked and destroyed Goguryeo's capital, Hwando' in 342; no border change is recorded.
wars.note: 355: Former Yan enfeoffed the Goguryeo king as duke of Lelang (Lelang page). The Former Yan dossier should carry any vassal relation.

wars.name: Baekje–Goguryeo war of 369-371
wars.outcome: Baekje repelled a Goguryeo invasion at Chiyang in 369 and in 371 'took the fortress of Pyongyang and killed Gogugwon of Goguryeo'; no border changed.
wars.note: Baekje's 371 move of its capital to Hansan is on the same page.

wars.name: Gwanggaeto's conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Ten walled cities in 392 and more land in 395; the Baekje capital taken and Asin submitted in 396.
wars.note: The Goguryeo page: Gwanggaeto 'defeated and subjugated Paekche'.

wars.name: Goguryeo expedition to Silla and Gaya
wars.outcome: Goguryeo drove out the Wa/Gaya pressure on Silla and made it a protectorate; 'Gaya declined and never recovered'.
wars.note: The page gives both 399 and 400 for the Silla request.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Later Yan war
wars.outcome: Later Yan attacks in 400, 405 and 406 failed; Goguryeo conquered all of Liaodong.
wars.note: Cliopatria's Later Yan shape loses 54,888 km2 in 407.

wars.name: Goguryeo's conquest of Hanseong
wars.outcome: Jangsu captured Wiryeseong and killed Gaero; Baekje moved to Ungjin.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Silla wars of Jangsu
wars.outcome: Parts of Gangwon in 468 and seven walled cities in North Gyeongsang in 489.

wars.name: Baekje–Silla campaign against Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Baekje retook its old capital in 551; Silla 'took possession of the entire Han River valley in 553'; King Seong of Baekje was killed in 554.
wars.note: The Seong page puts the Baekje–Silla–Gaya campaign in 551 to 553 and Seong's death in 554.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Sui War

zones.text: Liaodong and the Liao River line

wars.outcome: Goguryeo victory: 'Out of the initial 305,000 men ... only 2,700 returned'; 613 a second failure; 614 peace.
wars.note: The page dates the first Goguryeo strike 597 (infobox 598) and says Yeongyang 'gave up the buffer zone' before 612.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Tang War
wars.outcome: Taizong took Gaimou, Liaodong and Baiyan in 645 and withdrew on 13 October; Su Dingfang besieged Pyongyang in 661; Tang and Silla took Pyongyang on 22 October 668.
wars.note: The Goguryeo page has Taizong's 647 and 648 invasions 'defeated both times' and the Battle of Sasu in 662. The Silla–Tang page has the Protectorate General to Pacify the East at Pyongyang from 668.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders are recorded for Goguryeo. The Yalu and Liao rivers and the Taedong are natural lines only in outline; the Liaodong frontier moved with every war and the Han River frontier with every Baekje–Silla campaign.

notes:
Cliopatria rows and modelling choices.
1. The Goguryeo row (-36..681) is one state that ends 668 (Pyongyang, 22 October). Cliopatria keeps the 360,601 km2 shape to 673 and then a 148 km2 sliver to 681 (goguryeo_674, verdict wrong, correction an empty region). The Tang protectorate (668/669 to 676) and the Silla share south of the Taedong need the Tang and Silla dossiers; a dossier for the Protectorate General to Pacify the East may be wanted.
2. Start moved to 37 BCE (the page) from Cliopatria's 36 BCE; a one-year keyframe goguryeo_-37 covers it.
3. Dong-okjeo and the Ye are carried as Goguryeo vassals (56 and 53 on) and annexed 401, which is the Dongye dossier's bridging year for 'early 5th-century'; Cliopatria has them in Goguryeo's shape from 154 and 392. Every Goguryeo shape from 154 to 395 therefore has an adjust verdict that subtracts them. The 53 start for the Ye is confidence 1 (the page gives only Taejo's reign 53 to 146).
4. Counterparts without a dossier: buyeo (Buyeo, Eastern Buyeo/Dongbuyeo; annexed 22, 410, 491 here), lelang-commandery (jk-02-x), Northern Okjeo (Buk-okjeo), Biryu and Haengin (tribal, 'nobody' ids).
5. Nangnang 37 to 44 is the Daemusin page's 'Nakrang/Nangnang'; the Lelang page has Wang Zun restoring Han control in 30. The counterpart is han-dynasty.
6. The 612-616 dip (-52,939 km2) is read as the page's 'buffer zone' given up before 612; the Sui shape gains only 19,139 km2. Both the 612 loss and the 617 gain are confidence 1.
7. Silla gains 48,888 km2 in 555 reaching 40.16N (the east coast); the pages opened only give the Han River valley (553). A gap-filler should open the Silla pages for 551-568.
8. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none expected beyond the Natural Earth spellings used; the Jolbon/Huanren, Biryu and Haengin placements are placeholders. Pages that gave nothing: the 'Dongye' title (disambiguation).
9. No ruler list is given: the Goguryeo page has a king table that was not read; rulers omitted.
10. The Wei page (outcome): the Ye and Okjeo tributaries came under Lelang and Daifang's influence after 245; this is not drawn, because no page dates Goguryeo's recovery.
Counterpart events to be mirrored by other dossiers: Tang (contests 645, 667-668; protectorate), Baekje (mine), Silla (400-468 protectorate, 551-553, 468, 489 losses), Later Yan (405-406), Sui (612-617), Cao Wei (244-245), Han (32-44).
